looks.howToWear: Wear the shirt buttoned and half-tucked into the trousers, with the sleeves pushed to the elbow. Cuff the wide-leg trousers twice so the hems stay clear of puddles. Belt the trench loosely, or leave it open if it gets muggy. Keep the crossbody under the trench so the nylon stays dry. The cap brim keeps rain off your face.
looks.why: This is the co-ord you've only worn once, and it suits you: sage is on your palette and the wide leg is a relaxed shape you like. The matching set looks deliberate and more put-together than jeans and a tee. Linen dries fast, and the running shoes make hours of walking comfortable. No black sits near your face.

looks.title: Navy Shirt Dress, Rain Edit
looks.idea: One-piece dressing with a trench: easy, minimal and a step up, with nothing heavy to get soaked.
looks.howToWear: Button the dress to the chest and cinch it with the tan belt at the waist. Roll the sleeves to three-quarter length. Wear the trench open over it and let the navy show as a long column. Wear the Chelsea boots with bare ankles. Carry the leather tote on your shoulder, tucked under the trench if the rain gets heavy. Add the fine chain at the open collar.
looks.why: Navy is a flattering colour for you, and the straight belted shirt dress suits your broad shoulders and slim hips. The tan belt and gold add a bit of interest without being loud. The leather boots keep your feet dry. They're the warmest option, so swap to the running shoes if the humidity wins.

looks.title: Linen Shirt, Shorts and Trench
looks.idea: Your best everyday formula, adapted for a wet day: fresh and easy with no wet hems.
looks.howToWear: Wear the white linen shirt loose and untucked, with the cuffs rolled and the top button undone. Let the mid-thigh denim shorts sit just below the shirt hem. Wear the trench open or belted over the top. Add the chain and watch. Keep the sunglasses in the crossbody for when the rain eases.
looks.why: This is a variation on the white linen shirt and jeans combination that felt effortless for you. Shorts mean nothing heavy and wet clinging to your legs on a humid 21° day. Bare legs dry in minutes. Soft white near your face is flattering, and the trench keeps the look polished rather than beachy.

output.note: All three looks use the trench, because it's your only rain layer. You have no umbrella and no truly waterproof shoes. If you're walking in heavy rain, the running shoes are the safest bet. The white trainers and tan slides would stain and slip, so I left them out. Satin pieces like the cobalt skirt don't suit rain, so save that for a dry day.

failures.detail: s54 black mesh running shoes soak through in the first puddle, which is miserable on an all-day walking day. s51 leather Chelsea boots, or even s50 leather trainers, keep water out far better than mesh. Wide-leg linen s27 hems will still wick water even cuffed twice.
The 'Why' claims no black sits near her face, but the s66 black cap does exactly that and cuts the soft tonal sage-and-beige palette.
Double-cuffed wide-leg linen over chunky black athletic runners makes a stubby, bunched hem that fights the long, fluid line the co-ord is meant to give.
It is factually off on black at the face. It also calls mesh runners the rain-safe choice and never addresses wet linen creasing heavily.

looks.comment: This is the right instinct: s17 and s27 are an under-used co-ord in her best cool colour under the trench, and that is genuinely grown-up. But the black mesh runners and black cap undo both the practicality and the calm. Swap to s51, cuff the trousers to just above the boot and drop the cap, and this is the look.

failures.detail: The s60 black leather tote is large leather in all-day rain, and it cannot realistically be 'tucked under the trench'. The s61 nylon crossbody is the obvious rain bag. Wearing the trench open 'to show the column' in all-day rain also defeats the coat.
Telling her to swap to the running shoes if she gets hot undermines the most rain-sensible shoe choice. The mix of gold jewellery and a silver watch is not explained.

looks.comment: This is the most practically sound look: the s36 navy midi shirt dress and s51 leather Chelsea boots under a belted s44 is clean, flattering and walkable. The tan s68 belt picking up the trench is a nice quiet link. Swap the leather tote for s61 and tell her to belt the trench closed when it pours.

failures.detail: Mid-thigh s28 shorts under a knee-length s44 trench create the 'nothing underneath' effect. Bare legs then end in chunky black runners.
The white linen s07 goes sheer when rain-spotted with the trench worn open. The s54 mesh runners soak through. s67 sunglasses on a rain-all-day forecast are filler.
Denim shorts work against her stated aspiration to look more put-together and grown-up, especially for a day that may include the office.
It is not a repeat, but it leans on the s07 + jeans success while discarding what made it work: the long straight leg and the tan slides.
'Bare legs dry in minutes' is the only real logic. Nothing addresses sheer wet linen or the coat-over-shorts proportion.

looks.comment: Shorts under a knee-length trench with soaked mesh runners is a weekend errand compromise, not a grown-up rainy-day look. It reads as the weakest of the three and should be replaced, not tweaked.

judgement.missedOpportunity: s44 trench belted + s17 sage linen shirt + s27 sage linen trousers cuffed to just above the ankle + s51 black leather Chelsea boots + s61 nylon crossbody + s63 gold hoops + s65 watch. It is the same tonal sage idea with a shoe that actually keeps her dry and no black at the face.
judgement.summary: The stylist read the palette well and found the strongest under-used piece, the sage co-ord, along with a genuinely good navy shirt-dress option. The note about having no umbrella or waterproof shoes is honest and useful. But for a brief that is fundamentally 'walking all day in rain', the shoe logic is backwards. Mesh running shoes appear twice as the 'safest bet', when s51 leather Chelsea boots, and even s50 leather trainers, keep water out far better. Look 3 (shorts under a trench, white linen, sunglasses) should be cut. Look 2 is the only one ready to send, after swapping the leather tote for the nylon crossbody. All three lean on the same trench, which is fair given it is the only rain layer, but two looks also repeat the same wrong shoe, so the range is thinner than it appears.

results.requestText: First date — cocktails at a smart bar.

looks.title: Cobalt Hour
looks.idea: The never-worn cobalt satin skirt finally gets its moment, kept simple with a white tee so the colour does the talking.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the fitted white tee in fully so the bias-cut skirt sits at the natural waist. Drape the cream cardigan over your shoulders, unbuttoned, for the air-con and for a softer line. Wear the fine gold chain at the neckline and the small hoops. Add the silver watch and the silver flats, and keep the crossbody small and worn across the body.
looks.why: Cobalt is one of her flattering cool colours and it sits right by her face in a place that suits her. Satin plus a plain cotton tee is relaxed and minimal, like her COS and Toteme references, but a step up from her usual denim. The silver flats add a bit of interest without volume and keep her on flat shoes.

looks.title: Tonal Tailoring
looks.idea: Navy and dusty blue, sharp but unfussy: her only tailored trousers with an oversized shirt worn loose.
looks.howToWear: Tuck only the front of the oversized light blue shirt into the high-rise pleated trousers so the pleats show. Leave the back loose. Roll the sleeves to just below the elbow and open two buttons, with the gold chain sitting in the V. Add the small hoops and the silver watch, then finish with the black ballet flats and the crossbody.
looks.why: Navy and dusty blue are core colours for her, and the tonal pairing reads as grown-up without trying hard. The wide, straight trouser shape fits her broad shoulders and slim hips and keeps her comfortable. It's polished enough for a smart bar but still feels like her, and it's cool in the humidity.

looks.title: Sage Set, Dressed Up
looks.idea: The under-worn sage linen co-ord, styled as a quiet evening suit rather than a holiday set.
looks.howToWear: Wear the sage linen shirt open as a light jacket over the cream ribbed tank, with the sleeves pushed up to the forearm. Tuck the tank into the wide-leg trousers and cinch the drawstring so the waist is defined. Add the gold chain over the tank, the small hoops, the silver watch, the silver flats and the crossbody.
looks.why: Sage and cream are soft cool-leaning tones that suit her colouring, and she has only worn this set once. Splitting the set into an open shirt layer over a tank turns it from a beach co-ord into something interesting but still understated. It's breathable linen for 24°C and humid weather, with a long, easy line.

output.note: No heels, per her preference for flats outside weddings. I avoided black near her face. The wardrobe's only evening bag options are the large tote and the small black nylon crossbody. A small leather clutch or structured bag would sharpen all three looks.

failures.detail: Claims the cobalt 'sits right by her face' — s34 is a skirt; the colour at her face is white jersey. The reasoning is factually wrong about where the flattering colour lands.

A fitted cotton jersey tee (s02, formality 1) with the black nylon crossbody (s61) drags a smart-bar date look down. The tee-and-slip formula needs a crisper top here. Her proven white linen shirt (s07) or the light blue poplin (s08) would hold the satin better.

The cream cardigan (s42) draped over the shoulders adds bulk exactly where she is broadest, and it reads preppy rather than COS/Toteme. It should be carried or worn on, not knotted on top of broad shoulders.
Gold hoops and chain are mixed with a silver watch and silver flats with no stated intent. The mixed metals look accidental rather than styled.

looks.comment: The right instinct: finally wearing the never-worn cobalt skirt s34 with flat silver s56 is the most interesting thing this wardrobe can do for a date. But the explanation misplaces the colour, and s02 plus a shoulder-draped cardigan makes it read daytime-casual and broadens her top half.

failures.detail: Navy tailoring s30 plus blue shirt s08 is essentially her leadership-review outfit with hoops. It is polished but has no date-night charge, and nothing in it is for the evening.
Black round-toe flats (s52) and the nylon crossbody (s61) keep it office-flat. The pointed silver flats (s56) would sharpen it and give it an evening note.

looks.comment: Correct colour story and a good front-tuck to show the pleats on her slim hips, so it is a sendable, flattering look. But it feels like Tuesday at work rather than a first date, and a wool-blend trouser at 24°C and humid is the warmest option of the three.

failures.detail: The idea says 'quiet evening suit', but wearing s17 open over a ribbed tank with pushed sleeves is the holiday-set styling. That moves it toward beach, not toward a smart bar.
Tells her to 'cinch the drawstring' on s27. The drawstring belongs to the black linen trousers s26; s27 is listed only as relaxed wide-leg.
Minor point: the cream ribbed tank s13 leans warm at the neckline against her cool, low-contrast colouring. The sage shirt itself, buttoned up, would be better at the face.

looks.comment: Reviving the once-worn sage co-ord s17/s27 in breathable linen is smart for the humidity. But the styling undercuts the stated idea: wear the shirt buttoned and fully tucked, collar slightly open with the chain, so it reads as a soft suit rather than a resort set.

judgement.missedOpportunity: s34 cobalt satin midi skirt with s07 white linen shirt (her proven 'effortless' piece) tucked at the waist, sleeves rolled and collar open. Finish with s64 fine gold chain, s63 hoops, s56 silver pointed flats, and s42 cardigan carried for air-con. That is crisp, grown-up, interesting but not loud. Next best: s08 light blue shirt half-tucked into s34 for a tonal-blue version.
judgement.summary: The stylist found the right pieces: the never-worn cobalt skirt, her only tailoring, and the neglected sage co-ord. All three are cool-toned, black is kept off her face, and every look is in flats. Execution keeps slipping, though. Look 1 pairs the skirt with a casual fitted tee, adds a shoulder-draped cardigan that bulks her broad shoulders, and wrongly claims the cobalt sits at her face. Look 2 is flattering but is her work outfit. Look 3 styles the 'evening suit' the beachy way, and its drawstring instruction belongs to s26, not s27. The identical gold chain/hoops/silver watch/nylon crossbody kit across all three makes them feel samey, and the metals are mixed without comment. The stylist was right to flag that there is no proper evening bag. Fix the top in Look 1 and this goes from competent to genuinely good.

results.requestText: Weekend brunch and then wandering around the shops.

looks.title: Cobalt Satin and a White Tee
looks.idea: The never-worn cobalt skirt dressed down with the simplest white tee, so the colour does the talking.
looks.howToWear: Half-tuck the front of the boxy white tee into the skirt so the waist is defined but the shape stays relaxed. Let the skirt hang loose and bias-cut, no belt. Wear the silver flats with bare ankles. Add the fine gold chain, small hoops and silver watch, and carry the small crossbody across your body to keep your hands free for shopping.
looks.why: Cobalt is one of her flattering colours, and a plain white tee keeps it minimal rather than loud. It is the 'more interesting, but not loud' step she wants. It is also easy: a tee, a skirt and flats, in light fabrics that cope with humidity. The silver flats lift it out of casual without adding heel.

looks.title: Sage Linen, Split Up
looks.idea: The once-worn sage co-ord worn as separate, relaxed pieces so it feels easy rather than matchy.
looks.howToWear: Wear the sage shirt open and untucked over the fitted white tee, with the sleeves pushed to the elbow. Pull the wide-leg trousers up to sit at the waist and let them fall straight over the slides. Carry the straw tote. Keep the jewellery to small gold hoops and the silver watch, and wear the sunglasses.
looks.why: Sage is on her palette and linen is the best fabric for 24°C and humidity. Breaking up the set, with the white tee underneath, makes it look styled rather than like a uniform, and it brings out a piece she has barely worn. The long, relaxed lines suit her broad shoulders and slim hips, and it is very COS and Jenni Kayne.

looks.title: Navy Shirt Dress, Sneaker Edit
looks.idea: A belted navy shirt dress with white trainers: polished enough to look grown-up, easy enough for hours of walking.
looks.howToWear: Undo the top two buttons and roll the sleeves to just below the elbow. Belt the dress with the tan leather belt at the waist and blouse the bodice slightly. Leave the skirt falling straight to the midi length. Wear the white trainers, with the gold chain, hoops and silver watch. Carry the black tote for shopping bags.
looks.why: Navy is a flattering colour for her and keeps the face area soft, unlike black. A shirt dress is one piece and one decision, so it is quick on a weekend morning. The tan belt echoes the tan accent from her successful white shirt look, and the trainers keep it practical for the shops. It is more put-together than jeans and a tee but still clean and minimal.

output.note: Nothing is missing for this brief. Every look uses flats, avoids black near the face, and brings in a piece she rarely or never wears.

failures.detail: Says the look uses 'light fabrics that cope with humidity', but bias-cut satin (s34) is the least humidity-friendly thing here. It clings when damp, creases across the lap after an hour sitting at brunch and shows water marks. The client should be warned rather than reassured.

The black nylon crossbody (s61) is the sportiest, flattest note in the look and pulls against the satin and the pointed silver flats (s56). The jewellery also mixes gold at the face (s63, s64) with silver at the wrist (s65) and silver shoes, with no stated intent. For a cool, low-contrast client, all-silver or a deliberate mix would read as more considered.

looks.comment: This is the best look in the set. It finally puts the never-worn cobalt skirt (s34) to work with a boxy white tee half-tucked, and the silver pointed flats are a smart, cool-toned lift that suits her colouring. Two things hold it back: the humidity caveat on satin is missing, and the crossbody and metals are loosely chosen.

failures.detail: The title and the 'why' both claim the co-ord is 'split up' and 'worn as separate pieces'. In fact s17 and s27 are still worn together head to toe, with the shirt simply left open over s02. The client will notice that the promise and the outfit don't match.

The stated idea, breaking the set to make it feel less matchy, isn't actually carried out. Wearing the set open over a tee is pleasant, but it is the default way to wear a linen co-ord, not a new idea for this one.

looks.comment: As an outfit it's lovely and very Jenni Kayne: tonal sage linen, tan slides (s53) and the straw tote (s62) suit her colouring and the 24°C humidity. But it doesn't do what it says. Either rename it honestly as 'the set, softened with a white tee', or genuinely split it, for example s17 over s21 jeans.

failures.detail: A shirt dress with white trainers is the generic weekend answer. The tan-belt swap (s68) is the only real styling move.

The neutrals don't connect. The tan belt (s68) has nothing to echo it, while the black tote (s60) and the white trainers (s50) each sit alone against the navy. The 'echoes her successful look' reasoning works only on paper.

looks.comment: This is the reliable, practical option. Navy keeps black away from her face, the trainers suit hours of walking and the large tote holds shopping. It's competent rather than interesting, and the accessory colours feel picked one at a time rather than as a story.

judgement.missedOpportunity: Actually split the co-ord and rerun her proven formula in a new colour. Wear the sage linen shirt (s17) loose, half-tucked into the light-wash straight jeans (s21), with sleeves pushed up. Add the tan belt (s68), tan slides (s53), straw tote (s62), silver watch (s65) and small hoops (s63). This copies the structure of her known win (s07 + s21 + s53) but in sage, it's fully breathable linen and cotton, and it shows her the co-ord works as two wardrobe pieces.
judgement.summary: This is a good, client-appropriate edit that rightly reaches for under-used pieces (s34, s56, s17/s27, s36), keeps black away from her face and respects the flats directive. Look 1 is the standout: a genuine 'more interesting but not loud' step. It needs a satin-in-humidity caveat and a more deliberate bag and metal choice. Look 2 is a nice outfit, but its explanation is inaccurate: the co-ord is not split. That needs fixing before it goes out. Look 3 is safe and practical but forgettable. The set would rise from competent to excellent with an honest Look 2 that genuinely splits the co-ord, and with closer attention to accessory colour stories.

results.requestText: I'm presenting to senior leadership next week. I want to look authoritative but still like me.

looks.title: Navy Tailoring, Softened
looks.idea: Her one tailored trouser in a crisp blue shirt: authority through proportion and colour rather than a suit.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the front and sides of the oversized shirt into the high-rise pleated trousers and leave the back looser, so the shape stays relaxed. Undo one extra button and roll the sleeves to just below the elbow. Let the wide straight leg skim the ankle bone over the black flats. Keep the jewellery to the small gold hoops and the silver watch. Carry the tote.
looks.why: Navy and dusty blue suit her cool, low-contrast colouring, with no black near her face. The pleated trousers are the sharpest piece she owns and have only been worn 3 times. The look reads as put-together and grown-up but stays in the COS and Toteme territory she likes: clean, relaxed and minimal. The cotton poplin copes with humidity better than a jacket would.

looks.title: Sage Co-ord, Finally Worn
looks.idea: A tonal soft-green set that looks deliberate and quietly senior, with no effort needed.
looks.howToWear: Wear the set as a true two-piece. Tuck the shirt fully into the wide-leg trousers and loosen the drawstring so it sits flat and the waist looks clean. Leave the top button undone and roll the sleeves once or twice, neatly. Add the fine gold chain at the neckline. Steam the linen the night before so it looks crisp. Finish with the silver pointed flats and the black tote.
looks.why: This is her most under-used piece, worn once, and sage is a flattering colour for her. A single colour head to toe elongates her frame and softens her broad shoulders. Slim pointed silver flats add polish without a heel. It is the 'sharper version of her own style' look: relaxed linen, but one step up from white shirt and jeans.

looks.title: Cobalt Moment
looks.idea: Her never-worn cobalt skirt, with plain white and a blazer to keep it grown-up and a little interesting.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the fitted white tee fully into the bias-cut skirt, so it sits at the high waist and the skirt falls straight. Throw the oversized blazer over the top and push the sleeves up to the forearm so it looks slouchy rather than stiff. Wear the gold chain at the neckline, with the hoops and watch. The silver flats pick up the sheen of the satin. Keep the blazer on for the presentation and take it off when you're out in the heat.
looks.why: Cobalt is one of her best colours and gives the 'bit more interesting, not loud' she wants. White next to her face keeps things fresh, so the black blazer stays below the face and her tired-in-black problem is avoided. The oversized blazer gives her authority and balances her broad shoulders, while the slim satin skirt shows off her slim hips. The skirt has never been worn, and this look makes it work with plain basics she already owns.

output.note: Her wardrobe has only one tailored bottom (s30) and no blazer in a softer cool colour, as the only one is black. A grey or navy blazer would be the one buy that completes this brief. The black blazer is optional over looks 1 and 2 if the room is cold, but 24°C and humid means linen and poplin should do the job without it.

failures.detail: An oversized shirt front-tucked into high-rise pleats needs a waist line. The s68 tan belt would sharpen it and warm up the navy, and it was left out.
It doesn't address her broad shoulders. The oversized s08 may have a dropped shoulder that softens them or a boxy one that widens them, and the stylist should say which and how to check.

looks.comment: This is the right answer to the brief. s30 is her sharpest piece, s08 keeps soft cool blue at the face, and the half-tuck keeps it relaxed rather than corporate. Swapping the black s52 for the silver s56 and adding the s68 belt would take it from strong to finished.

failures.detail: Fully tucking a relaxed linen shirt into a drawstring wide-leg trouser and loosening the drawstring exposes a gathered, pyjama-like waist. It is the opposite of 'clean'. A front tuck, or wearing s17 open as an overshirt, would sit better.
Linen steamed the night before will be creased after a humid commute and a morning of sitting. That undercuts 'authoritative' at the moment she stands up to present.
A single colour elongates her frame but does nothing to 'soften broad shoulders'. That claim is filler.

looks.comment: Very her, and it finally activates the s17/s27 set with flattering sage and the s56 pointed flats. As a presentation look, though, it is the softest of the three and needs a better waist solution. It works best as the 'still like me' option for a relaxed room.

failures.detail: The black s40 blazer's lapels and shoulders frame her face directly. The claim that black 'stays below the face' is wrong, and this is exactly the harsh black she looks tired in.
A polyester blazer at 24°C and humid is uncomfortable. The plan to take it off outside leaves a fitted tee and a satin skirt.
A bias-cut satin s34 slip skirt reads as after-work drinks rather than a leadership review. Satin also shows sweat marks and creases under stress and heat.
A fitted tee with a clinging bias-cut skirt goes against her preference for relaxed, straight shapes. The boxy s01 tee would at least be hers.
An oversized blazer adds width to broad shoulders; it doesn't 'balance' them. The reasoning contradicts her body notes.

looks.comment: Styling the never-worn cobalt skirt is a worthy goal, but this is the wrong occasion for it. The look also reintroduces black at the face while claiming to avoid it. Save s34 for after-work drinks.

judgement.missedOpportunity: s36 navy midi shirt dress belted with s68 tan belt, s56 silver pointed flats, s63 hoops, s65 watch and s60 tote. It puts navy at the face, is breathable cotton for 24°C, and is a relaxed button-through midi that reads authoritative and grown-up in flats. It is a far stronger second presentation option than the cobalt satin look.
judgement.summary: Look 1 is a genuinely good answer. It builds on her only tailored piece in flattering cool blues, needs only a belt and the silver flats to be excellent, and is the look I'd lead with. Look 2 is true to her and puts the unused co-ord to work, but linen and a drawstring tuck soften the authority, and the creasing risk needs handling. Look 3 fails the brief: a black blazer at the face, polyester in humid heat, and an evening satin skirt for a leadership review, defended with inaccurate reasoning about colour and shoulders. The stylist's note honestly identifies the missing softer-coloured blazer, which I credit. The navy shirt dress (s36) was the obvious missed option.

results.requestText: Wedding guest — outdoor afternoon ceremony, and the forecast says it might rain.

looks.title: Cobalt Satin Afternoon
looks.idea: The cobalt skirt finally gets its moment, kept quiet with soft cream and minimal gold.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the cream ribbed tank in at the waist so the bias-cut skirt falls straight from the hip. Wear the fine gold chain and small hoops, with nothing else on top. Silver flats pick up the sheen of the satin. Carry the trench over your arm, and belt it loosely if it showers. Wear sunglasses for the ceremony.
looks.why: Cobalt is one of her best colours and it lights up her blue eyes. Cream next to her face is softer than black or stark white. The shape is a straight column with no cling, so it stays relaxed and minimal but looks clearly dressed up. The satin skirt has never been worn, and this is the right occasion for it.

looks.title: Soft Tailoring
looks.idea: Navy wide-leg trousers and a crisp pale blue shirt: grown-up and polished, still easy.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the oversized shirt fully into the high-rise pleated trousers, then pull a little out at the waist so it blouses. Undo two buttons and roll the sleeves to just below the elbow. Add the tan belt, gold hoops, fine chain and silver watch. Wear the black ballet flats. The trench goes over the top for rain.
looks.why: This is her version of COS or Toteme tailoring, in navy and dusty blue, which are both in her palette. The wide, straight trouser suits her broad shoulders and slim hips. It is wedding-appropriate without a dress, and it handles humidity and rain well. The look is also a step up from her usual jeans and tee.

looks.title: Sage Linen Set
looks.idea: A tonal co-ord worn as a deliberate, quiet suit: easy, clean, and a bit more interesting.
looks.howToWear: Wear the set together. Button the shirt, leave the top two open, and tuck it in loosely at the front only. Roll the sleeves once or twice and let the wide-leg trousers sit full length over the flats. Add gold hoops and the fine chain. Steam the linen the night before. If rain is forecast, wear the trench over it on the way in and take it off for the ceremony.
looks.why: Sage is a soft cool colour that flatters her, and the set has only been worn once. It looks deliberate and put-together rather than pieced together. The relaxed wide-leg shape is what she's most comfortable in, and linen is the best fabric for 24°C and humidity.

output.note: The silver ballet flats and black ballet flats are your only suitable flat dress shoes, so the three looks share them. Pick the pair that suits the day. The 8cm stiletto sandals aren't suitable for grass and rain, and they're not a low heel, so I left them out. Your wardrobe has no dressy clutch, so the small black crossbody is the best option, and there's no umbrella. I'd avoid the white broderie dress, since white can compete with the bride, and the black satin pieces, since black near your face looks harsh. A small silver or neutral clutch would round out the wedding looks.

failures.detail: The slim cream ribbed tank s13 (formality 1/5) bares and narrows the top half. That draws the eye straight to her broad shoulders and drops the register below the satin. The bottom half says wedding and the top says gym-to-brunch.
'Cobalt lights up her blue eyes' is a stretch, because the cobalt sits at her hips, not her face. The tip to wear sunglasses s67 for the ceremony is also a misstep: they come off for the vows.

The black nylon crossbody s61 is the most casual piece in the look. It isn't softened or addressed. Gold hoops and chain with silver flats is an unexamined metal mix. For her cool colouring, the silver watch s65 would have tied the look to the shoes.

looks.comment: Anchoring on the never-worn cobalt s34 is exactly the right instinct for this brief, and the cream is kind to her face. But the rib tank is too slight and too casual. Swap in the light blue poplin s08, tucked with sleeves rolled, for a tonal-blue look that covers the shoulders and feels Toteme. That would make it a signature look.

failures.detail: Navy pleated trousers s30, an oversized poplin shirt, a tan belt and black flats read as a leadership-review outfit, not a wedding guest. Nothing here signals celebration.
This is her work uniform stepped up, not an occasion look. The silver flats s56 would have added at least one festive note in place of the black ballet flats s52.
The tan belt s68 sits between black flats and a black bag s61. The gold chain sits against a silver watch. None of these mixes is explained or tied together.
It claims a wool-blend trouser 'handles humidity well' at 24°C humid, which is debatable. 'Step up from jeans and tee' is about the office, not the occasion.

looks.comment: Navy and pale blue sit well on her colouring, and the bloused tuck is good technique. But this is a smart-office outfit, and it duplicates the shirt that should have been rescuing Look 1.

failures.detail: The black nylon crossbody s61 punctures a soft tonal sage-and-silver look. The silver watch s65 is missing, and it would echo the silver flats s56 better than adding more gold.

looks.comment: This is the strongest look: the once-worn sage co-ord s17/s27 as a quiet suit is pure Jenni Kayne. It's right for the heat, flattering at the face and comfortable. The steaming tip shows real-world thinking, and the trench s44 handles the rain. It only needs a cleaner bag solution and silver rather than gold to feel fully polished.

judgement.missedOpportunity: s34 cobalt satin skirt + s08 light blue oversized shirt, tucked and bloused with sleeves rolled + s56 silver flats + s65 silver watch + s63 hoops + s44 trench for showers. This is tonal cool blues, covers the broad shoulders, and has satin-meets-poplin ease. It's the grown-up, quietly interesting wedding look she has been missing.
judgement.summary: The stylist found the right pieces: the unworn cobalt skirt, the sage co-ord, the silver flats and the shower-resistant trench. The stylist's note is admirably honest about the missing clutch and umbrella, and about why the stilettos, black satin and white broderie are out. Execution is uneven. Look 1 undercuts the skirt with a casual slim tank that exposes her shoulders. Look 2 is an office outfit dressed as a wedding look and steals the shirt that would have perfected Look 1. Only Look 3 is ready to send. Across all three, the black nylon bag and the habitual gold-plus-silver mix go unexamined.

results.requestText: How should I wear my cobalt satin midi skirt (s34)?

looks.title: Cobalt, Kept Easy
looks.idea: Let the skirt be the one bold note against the crisp white basics she already wears all the time.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the front of the boxy white tee into the skirt, leaving the back loose, so the waist is defined and the boxy shape stays. Wear the skirt high on the waist so it falls straight and long. The white trainers keep it casual, so the satin reads as relaxed rather than dressy. Add the gold hoops, silver watch and sunglasses, and carry the crossbody.
looks.why: It's close to her white tee and jeans formula, with the skirt in place of the jeans. White next to cobalt looks clean and suits her cool, low-contrast colouring. The satin gives her a more grown-up, interesting piece without any fuss, and it works as a first, low-risk way to wear it for office days or brunch.

looks.title: The Linen Shirt, Dressed Up
looks.idea: Her proven white linen shirt and tan slides formula, with the skirt replacing jeans for a fresher weekend look.
looks.howToWear: Roll the linen sleeves to the elbow and tuck the shirt loosely into the skirt, with a soft blouse at the waist. Leave the top two buttons open and let the fine gold chain sit in the V. Wear the tan slides and carry the straw tote. The matt linen against the satin gives a nice contrast in texture.
looks.why: This repeats what has already worked for her: white linen shirt, tan slides, an easy and fresh feel. The skirt lifts it from jeans to something a bit more considered. Linen is breathable in 24°C humidity, and the flat sandals suit a weekend brunch or beach day.

looks.title: Blue on Blue
looks.idea: A tonal take that looks polished and quiet, with light blue poplin against deep cobalt.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the oversized light blue shirt fully into the skirt, then pull it out a little for a soft blouse. Roll the sleeves just below the elbow and leave the collar open. Wear the silver ballet flats and carry the black tote. Keep the jewellery minimal with the gold hoops and the silver watch.
looks.why: Dusty and light blues are in her best colour range, and the tonal pairing feels deliberate without being loud. The oversized shirt suits her broad shoulders, and the flats keep it practical and comfortable. It's her most put-together option for a leadership review or presentation, and the black blazer (s40) can go over it if the office aircon is cold.

output.note: No heels are needed. The skirt works with her flat shoes and basics. All three looks avoid black near her face. Her black blazer (s40) is the only outer layer I'd add for formal days, but it's too warm to wear in the 24°C humidity. A pale grey or navy top would be a useful addition to her wardrobe for wearing with the skirt.

failures.detail: The tee-and-trainers-with-a-slip-skirt formula is the most predictable answer. It is correct for a first wear, but the stylist then repeats the white-top idea in Look 2.

There are no notes on how a hip-length boxy cotton tee sits when front-tucked into bias satin. It needs a shallow tuck, or a tuck into the waistband only, to avoid a bulge over the hips. There is also no comment on mixing gold hoops (s63) with the silver watch (s65) on a cool-toned client.

looks.comment: This is a sound, wearable first outing for s34. The s01 boxy tee and s50 trainers make the satin feel easy, and white beside cobalt flatters her cool colouring. The idea is generic rather than sharpened for her.

failures.detail: The stylist pitches it for a 'beach day'. A satin midi skirt (s34) at the beach in humidity is not practical, and sand and water will mark the fabric. It is a brunch look, not a beach look.
This is essentially Look 1 again: a white top over the cobalt skirt with gold hoops. It only swaps the tee for the s07 shirt and the trainers for s53 slides, so it adds little range.
The tan belt (s68) would tie in the tan slides (s53) and straw tote (s62) and neaten a tucked linen shirt over bias satin, but it is ignored.

looks.comment: This look builds intelligently on her proven s07 + s53 formula. The matt-linen-against-satin texture note is genuinely good, as is the gold chain in the open V. It is let down by the beach claim and by how close it sits to Look 1.

failures.detail: Fully tucking a stiff oversized poplin shirt (s08) into a bias-cut satin skirt adds bulk and ridges at the hip, where satin shows everything. It also adds volume to her already broad shoulders. A half-tuck with a front knot, or sleeves pushed up and the shirt worn open over a fitted base, would balance it.

It says the black blazer (s40) can go over for aircon, but the note then calls it too warm. It is also black, right at her face, which contradicts the 'no black near her face' claim. The statement that an oversized shirt 'suits her broad shoulders' is asserted, not reasoned.
The suggested s40 black blazer layer puts harsh black at her face, which her profile explicitly flags as ageing.

looks.comment: Light blue against cobalt is the most interesting idea in the set, and the silver flats (s56) are a smart use of an under-worn piece. The full-tuck instruction and the black-blazer advice need fixing before this goes out.

judgement.missedOpportunity: The stylist says she should buy a pale grey or navy top, but she already owns both. s03 grey marl tee, half-tucked into s34 with s56 silver flats, s65 silver watch and s64 fine chain, is a soft-cool, very Toteme take for office days. The more 'interesting but not loud' option was s17 sage linen shirt worn open and knotted at the waist over s13 cream tank with s34 and s53 slides. Sage against cobalt is a quiet, grown-up colour pairing, and it would revive the once-worn co-ord shirt.
judgement.summary: These are competent, wearable recommendations that respect her flats directive and steer away from black, but the set is safe. Two of the three looks are white top plus cobalt skirt, and the beach suggestion is impractical. Look 3 has the best idea but the weakest execution: a bulky full tuck and contradictory black-blazer advice. Most damaging, the note tells her to buy a grey or navy top she already owns (s03, s05), which shows the stylist did not mine the wardrobe. Sage (s17) and the tan belt (s68) were also left on the table.

results.requestText: Long travel day tomorrow — I want to be comfortable but still look put-together.

looks.title: Sage Linen Set, Travel Edition
looks.idea: A tonal sage co-ord that looks planned, not thrown on, and is as comfortable as loungewear.
looks.howToWear: Wear the sage shirt open like a light jacket over the white fitted tee, with the front hem of the tee loosely tucked into the drawstring waist. Roll the shirt sleeves to just below the elbow. Keep the trousers full length and let them skim the top of the trainers. Carry the cream cardigan in the tote for the cold cabin and drape it over your shoulders at the gate. Add the gold hoops and silver watch, nothing else.
looks.why: This is your most under-worn piece (worn once), and it's ideal for a long day: breathable in 24° humidity, with loose linen that won't dig in after hours of sitting. Sage is one of your flattering cool colours, and the matching set reads polished while you're still in easy, straight shapes. Linen will crease, but on a travel day that looks relaxed and intentional. White trainers handle airport walking.

looks.title: Soft Tailoring, Zero Effort
looks.idea: Wide navy trousers with a white tee and a pale blue shirt: quietly grown-up and still easy.
looks.howToWear: Tuck only the front of the white boxy tee into the high-rise pleated trousers so the waist is defined and the trousers sit properly. Wear the light blue oversized shirt open over the top with the sleeves pushed up. Wear the fine gold chain at the neckline. Keep the trainers clean and white, and put your passport and essentials in the tote so your hands stay free.
looks.why: The navy pleated trousers are your only tailored bottom and have only been worn three times. The wide, straight cut is as comfortable as jeans but looks much more put-together. Navy, white and pale blue are all flattering cool tones near your face, with no black to tire you out. The open shirt gives you an extra layer for the air-con, and the whole look stays in the clean, minimal COS/Toteme space you like.

looks.title: The Easy Shirt Dress
looks.idea: A navy shirt dress with tan accents: one piece, nothing to coordinate, and a bit more interesting than jeans.
looks.howToWear: Button the dress to the sternum and leave the lower buttons open for stride room. Swap the dress's own belt for the tan leather belt, worn at the natural waist and not too tight, so you can sit comfortably. Wear the denim jacket on your shoulders or put it on for the cold cabin. Wear the crossbody across your body for hands-free airport moves, and add the gold hoops and chain. The tan slides slip off easily at security. If you'll be doing a lot of walking, swap to the white leather trainers (s50).
looks.why: A single piece in breathable cotton is the most comfortable option in humid heat, and the midi length looks composed after hours in transit. Navy with tan and denim echoes the effortless feel of your white shirt, jeans and tan slides combination, which has worked for you before. The belt and gold jewellery add the sharper, grown-up detail you're after without being loud.

output.note: I don't know where you're flying to, so I've kept every look layered for cold cabins and 24° humidity. If the destination is cooler, the cream cardigan or black leather jacket would be good additions. I left out the cobalt satin skirt for this brief: it's a lovely piece but better saved for after-work drinks or a wedding-guest outfit than a long-haul day.

failures.detail: s02 fitted tee under the open shirt goes against her stated preference for relaxed, straight shapes. The s01 boxy tee would sit more easily under s17 and is kinder over hours of sitting.

It never explains why breaking the co-ord into an open-shirt layer beats wearing it as a buttoned set, which is the actual styling move. It also doesn't address the heavy black s60 tote against an all-pale, tonal palette.

looks.comment: This is the right answer to the brief. It pulls the once-worn s17/s27 set into service in her best cool colour, is breathable at 24° and humid, and the cream s42 cardigan for the cabin is a smart, practical touch. I'd swap s02 for s01 and it's ready to send.

failures.detail: s30 is a wool-blend, pleated, fixed-waist trouser in 24° humidity. After a long day of sitting it will be warmer and less forgiving than the drawstring linen, and the pleats will crumple. Claiming it is 'as comfortable as jeans' is overselling it.

Putting the s08 oversized shirt over the s01 boxy tee stacks volume on her broad shoulders. A half-buttoned or knotted shirt, or just the tee with s42 over the shoulders, would balance the wide trouser better.

It repeats Look 1's formula almost exactly: open shirt over a white tee, wide trousers, white trainers, black tote, hoops, watch and sunglasses. It is effectively a colourway swap, not a different look.

looks.comment: The palette is right: navy, white and pale blue with no black at the face. Using her only tailored bottom is a good instinct for 'grown-up'. But fabric comfort and range are weak, and the look has too much in common with Look 1.

failures.detail: A belted, button-through dress left open below for stride is fiddly on a long travel day. Cramped seats, legs cold in the cabin and gaping buttons are all likely. The s53 slides also leave feet exposed on long walks, which the stylist half-admits by suggesting s50 as a swap.
The s61 black nylon crossbody breaks the tan story set up by s68 and s53. The mid-blue s41 trucker over the navy s36 is a near-miss blue-on-blue that looks casual rather than deliberate.

Linking this to her white linen shirt, jeans and slides success is a stretch, since the only shared element is the tan slides. The look also isn't really 'more interesting than jeans'; it is just more fiddly for this brief.

looks.comment: Navy is flattering and the tan belt is a real move. But a shirt dress is the least practical silhouette for this brief, and the accessories don't hold together. I'd replace it rather than send it.

judgement.missedOpportunity: A genuinely different third look built on her proven formula: s21 light-wash straight jeans, s07 white linen shirt (half-tucked), s68 tan belt, s50 white trainers, s42 cream cardigan for the cabin, s63 hoops and s64 chain, with s62 straw tote only if it's a holiday trip. It is comfortable, already proven to work in real life, and different in feel from the two wide-trouser looks. In the stylist's note, s44 beige trench should have replaced the s43 black leather jacket as the cooler-destination layer: shower-resistant and flattering, rather than black near the face.
judgement.summary: Look 1 is a strong, client-specific answer that finally gets the unworn sage co-ord into use, and it could go out with one small swap. Look 2 is the right palette but the wrong fabric for a long humid travel day, and it repeats Look 1's formula. Look 3 is the weakest on practicality and cohesion. The stylist correctly avoided black near the face and the cobalt satin, but recommending the black leather jacket in the note contradicts her colouring brief when the trench was available.

results.requestText: What should I wear to work tomorrow?

checks.detail: Shares most of its clothing with look 1.
Shares most of its clothing with look 2.

looks.title: Black-out cargo
looks.idea: Head-to-toe black utility: the easiest way to meet the café's plain-black rule on a bike in the cold.
looks.howToWear: Wear the band tee inside out so the print drops to a faint ghost and it reads close to plain black. Keep it untucked and boxy over the cargos, with the legs worn straight over the boots. Put the cropped puffer on for the ride and leave it in the staff area. The tote carries the rest.
looks.why: The cargos are the only plain black bottom that works with a full day on the bike. They are warm, they won't catch the wind, and they keep her undone, streetwear shape with the boxy tee over relaxed legs and chunky boots. The cropped puffer is the warmest layer she has for 4°C and wind, and it stays off at work.

looks.title: Slip and boots
looks.idea: A black satin slip dress roughed up with tights and chunky boots: Berlin club-kid sharpness for a shift behind the counter.
looks.howToWear: Wear the opaque tights under the slip dress with the lace-up boots, and the silver chain at the neck. Before cycling, knot the hem at one hip or tuck a handful of fabric into the tights so the bias cut doesn't flap in the wind, then release it at work. Pull the puffer over the top and zip it fully. The thin straps and satin will be cold on the ride without it.
looks.why: The slip is the only fully plain black piece that is a complete outfit, so it satisfies the dress code best. Pairing soft satin with heavy boots and a chunky chain is the 90s grunge and club mix she wears well. The 80 denier tights and the puffer cover the 4°C ride. The hem knot keeps it safe to cycle in.

looks.title: Tee over slip
looks.idea: A faded band tee thrown over the slip dress: a 90s grunge layer, mostly black, with the music showing.
looks.howToWear: Layer the boxy, faded band tee over the slip dress so the satin hem hangs out below it. Knot the tee at the side if the hem needs shortening for the bike. Wear the tights and boots, add the chain over the tee neckline, and zip the puffer on top for the ride.
looks.why: It is her style balance of an oversized top against something fitted and short, and the tee is the piece she wears most. The mix of cotton and satin looks undone rather than polished. It is mostly black, with only the print breaking it up. The tights, boots and puffer keep her warm on the walk and cycle.

output.note: Her wardrobe has no plain black top, and the café dress code is plain black. The band tee is the closest piece, and it is best worn inside out (look 1) or under a slip dress, which will be mostly plain black. Check whether the café supplies an apron or a uniform top. If not, a plain black tee or long-sleeve top would be the most useful buy, as it would make the cargo look fully compliant and cheaper to repeat.

failures.detail: At 4°C in a cold wind, a short-sleeve cotton tee under a cropped puffer (l10) is thin for the ride. The cropped hem also rides up at the back when she leans over the handlebars. The grey hoodie (l01) under the puffer for the commute, taken off in the staff area, was the obvious fix, and grey hood showing under a cropped puffer is good streetwear proportion too.
She could wear the opaque tights (l13) under the cargos (l06) as a windproof base layer for the bike. The chain (l14) could go on after the shift for the bar. Neither is mentioned.

looks.comment: This is the only look that genuinely answers 'plain black for a café shift on a bike'. Wearing the band tee (l02) inside out is a clever, honest workaround, and the black cargos with boots keep her streetwear shape. It needs a proper commute layer to be fully finished.

failures.detail: A bias-cut satin midi (l08) is wrong behind a café counter. Satin water-marks with every splash of milk or coffee, and thin straps slip while she carries and wipes. The l14 chain hangs into the work as well.
She has to cycle in everything. Knotting a bias-cut midi or stuffing it into tights is a fragile hack. The fabric will crease and twist, and loose satin near a chain or wheel is a real risk.
Bare arms and thin satin at 4°C. Once the puffer comes off at work she has nothing on her arms, and the warmth rating is 1/5.
This is a club-night outfit (formality 3/5) sent to a day shift. The 'Berlin club-kid' idea belongs to her evenings, not to work.
'Satisfies the dress code best' ignores that the dress code is only part of the brief. The job, the bike and the cold matter just as much.

looks.comment: The satin-with-boots mix is her taste, but this is the wrong day for it. It is cold, fragile and hard to cycle in, and the slip dress (l08) is wrong for café work. It should be saved for a gig.

failures.detail: The band tee (l02) is worn print-out here, which breaks the plain-black dress code more openly than Look 1 does. The stylist had just solved that problem by turning the tee inside out.
It keeps every cycling and café problem of the satin midi (l08): stains, flapping hem, knotting it for the bike.
The explanation claims 'oversized top against something fitted and short'. But the slip is a midi, so a boxy tee over a midi gives long-over-long with no short or fitted counterweight.
There is only short-sleeve cotton over satin indoors, and the same cold-ride exposure as Look 2.
Saying the tee is 'the piece she wears most' is not a reason it suits work. The explanation also misstates the proportion.

looks.comment: As a 90s grunge layer this is very her, but it belongs at a gig, not a café shift. It mostly duplicates Look 2 with the dress-code breach made more visible.

judgement.missedOpportunity: The full commute-to-counter version of Look 1. Wear l06 black cargos with l13 tights underneath as a wind base, and l02 band tee inside out. On the bike, put l01 grey hoodie under l10 cropped puffer, with the grey hem showing below the crop, and peel both off in the staff room. Finish with l11 boots and l15 tote, which can carry l14 chain for after the shift.
judgement.summary: The stylist read the core constraint correctly: there is no plain black top. The note says so honestly and names the right purchase, a plain black tee or long-sleeve. That deserves credit. Look 1 is a smart, practical answer, but it lacks a warm layer for the ride. Looks 2 and 3 are forced variety. They put a satin slip dress (l08) into a café shift and onto a bike at 4°C, which fails the job, the weather and her cycling directive. Look 3 also shows the print the dress code forbids. Both are really gig outfits. A stronger send would have been one fully finished work look with a commute layering plan, plus the honest shopping note.

results.requestText: Dinner with friends at a nice restaurant on Saturday night.

looks.title: Slip Dress, Undone
looks.idea: Satin slip dress roughed up with a cropped puffer and chunky boots, the 90s grunge way to dress up.
looks.howToWear: Wear the white ribbed tank under the slip dress so the tank straps and neckline peek out, a layered 90s look that also adds warmth. Put the black tights on underneath, then the lace-up boots, with the midi hem skimming the top of the boot shaft. Wear the cropped puffer open so the dress falls long below it, which keeps the proportion short over long. Let the silver chain sit over the tank and slip neckline. Carry the tote.
looks.why: This is the dressiest thing she owns, and it gets there through texture contrast rather than polish, so it doesn't turn corporate. The black, white and silver palette suits her high-contrast colouring. The bias-cut dress, opaque tights and chunky boots are fine to cycle in, and the puffer handles the cold wind on the ride.

looks.title: Tartan and Forest
looks.idea: Her favourite gig formula (oversized top, tartan mini, tights, boots) turned up a notch for dinner by swapping the hoodie for the green knit.
looks.howToWear: Tuck only the front of the chunky green jumper into the tartan skirt and let the back hang loose, which keeps the oversized top balanced against the short skirt. Wear the black opaque tights and lace-up boots, and push the jumper sleeves up to the forearm. Put the vintage leather jacket over the top, left open, with the silver chain sitting on the knit neckline.
looks.why: It repeats what has worked for her in spirit: a big top, a short A-line skirt, tights and boots. The deep green and red both suit her colouring. The wool knit, wool skirt and tights are warm enough for 4°C. It is the most comfortable look for walking and cycling, and the tartan and leather jacket keep it vintage-grunge rather than neat.

looks.title: All Black, Brown Leather
looks.idea: Black-on-black band tee and cargos, with the vintage leather jacket adding warmth and a dressed-up undone feel.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the boxy band tee fully into the cargo trousers to define the waist, and let the relaxed leg fall over the top of the boots without bunching. Wear the leather jacket on the shoulders with the collar up, and layer the silver chain over the tee so it is visible. Carry the tote.
looks.why: It is the most casual of the three and the closest to her Berlin club style. The tonal black and the faded music tee give the head-to-toe darkness she likes, and the brown jacket adds vintage warmth. On the windiest ride swap the leather jacket for the black puffer, as the tee is only a light layer. It is easy to cycle in.

output.note: Her wardrobe has no dressy shoes or smart layers, but that suits her style, so dinner is handled through texture, layering and the slip dress rather than polish. If the restaurant is properly dressy, Look 1 is the safest choice.

failures.detail: The cropped puffer (l10) is styled open, but at 4°C in a cold wind she needs it zipped on the bike; with only satin and a rib tank (l03) underneath, her chest will be very cold. There is also no advice on cycling in a bias-cut satin midi (l08), such as knotting or hitching the hem away from the chain.
Says the bias-cut dress is 'fine to cycle in' without any how-to. The tote (l15) is carried by default with no reasoning, and it is a heavy, casual note on her one dressy look.

looks.comment: This is the right anchor: it finally gets the under-worn slip dress (l08, worn 3x) out, and the tank-under-slip, tights and boots formula is true 90s grunge and true to Lena. It needs a zip-up instruction and a hem fix for the ride, and the dress could take a warmer layer over it.

failures.detail: Red tartan (l07) with a forest-green cable knit (l04) can read preppy or festive, which she has said would betray her style. Only the boots and leather jacket pull it back toward grunge, and the stylist never addresses the risk.

Front-tucking a chunky cable jumper into a wool A-line mini puts bulk at the waist and hip. A loose, untucked knit over the short skirt is the cleaner big-over-short balance. The chain (l14) on a cable-knit neckline also gets lost in the texture.
Claims the look is 'turned up a notch for dinner' but swapping hoodie for jumper barely changes the register. It also doesn't address red, green and brown (l09) together.

looks.comment: This is a sensible riff on her proven gig formula and the warmest look offered, with colours that suit her. But it is barely dressier than the hoodie version, and the tartan-plus-cable combination edges toward preppy unless the knit is worn loose and slouchy.

failures.detail: A band tee (l02) and cargos (l06) is her everyday studio and club uniform. The stylist even calls it 'the most casual of the three', which does not answer 'a nice restaurant on Saturday night'.
A cotton tee under a warmth-3 leather jacket (l09) at 4°C with a cold wind is underdressed. The stylist admits it and suggests swapping to the puffer, which undermines the look's own idea.
'Wear the leather jacket on the shoulders' cannot be done on a bike, which breaks the cycling directive in practice.
Fully tucking a boxy, faded tee into relaxed cargos loses the oversized-over-fitted balance she likes, leaving her with a shapeless, all-relaxed silhouette.
This is a default outfit with a chain added rather than a considered dinner look.

looks.comment: It sounds like her but doesn't answer the brief: too casual, too cold, and the jacket-on-shoulders styling ignores the bike. This slot should have been a second, warmer route into the slip dress.

judgement.missedOpportunity: Layer the forest green chunky jumper (l04) over the satin slip dress (l08), worn loose so about a hand's width of satin falls below the knit hem. Add the black opaque tights (l13), lace-up boots (l11) and silver chain (l14), with the black cropped puffer (l10) zipped for the ride. Deep green at the face suits her high-contrast colouring, the satin-against-cable texture clash is pure 90s grunge, and it is warm enough for 4°C both on the bike and inside. A band-tee-under-slip version (l02 under l08, with l09) would also have been a stronger third look than the cargos.
judgement.summary: Look 1 is the right answer: it uses the under-worn slip dress with authentic grunge layering, and the stylist's note honestly flags that the wardrobe lacks dressy shoes or smart layers. Look 2 is a reasonable but only slightly elevated repeat of her gig outfit, with an unaddressed preppy risk and an awkward bulky tuck. Look 3 is too casual and too cold, and its jacket-on-the-shoulders styling ignores the cycling directive. All three repeat the same boots, chain and tote, so the range feels narrow. Most importantly, the stylist never tried the slip dress with the green jumper or the band tee, which would have given two genuinely different, warm, dinner-worthy looks. Fix Look 1's practicalities (zip the puffer, deal with the hem for the bike) and replace Look 3 before sending.

results.requestText: Surprise me — put together something I wouldn't normally think of.

looks.title: Satin Under Fleece
looks.idea: Soft slip dress under a scruffy hoodie: the satin-against-sweatshirt mix of Berlin club style.
looks.howToWear: Pull the grey hoodie on over the slip dress and leave it loose, so the satin midi hem drops 15cm or more below the hoodie hem. Put the opaque tights on under the dress and lace the boots tight. Wear the cropped puffer on top, so you get three hems stacked at different lengths: puffer, then fleece, then satin. Let the hood sit outside the puffer collar and wear the chain over the hoodie. If the dress flaps while you cycle, hitch it up a little through the hoodie. The tights and boots keep your legs covered.
looks.why: The slip dress has only been worn 3 times, and this makes it an everyday piece instead of a going-out one. Oversized on top with a fluid, narrow shape underneath is the balance you like. It also draws on your grunge references, with the slip over a hoodie as a 90s move. The hoodie, tights, boots and puffer keep it warm for 4°C and wind, and the boots and tights make it safe for walking and cycling.

looks.title: Tartan, Turned Down
looks.idea: Red tartan and forest green in an undone, scruffy mix that looks like a worn-in 90s band tee and not a Christmas outfit.
looks.howToWear: Pull the chunky green jumper on loose and tuck only a small section at the front into the mini skirt, so the back and sides stay bulky. Wear the black tights and the retro green and white trainers, which pick up the green of the jumper. Put the boxy leather jacket on open and let the jumper hem hang out under it. Wear the chain over the jumper neckline, and shove the tote on a shoulder or hang it off the handlebars.
looks.why: The tartan skirt is under-worn at 6 wears and is your best piece for gigs. Red and deep green both suit your high-contrast colouring. The trainers, the scruffy leather jacket and the loose, partly tucked jumper stop it reading as festive or preppy. The big jumper over a short skirt gives you the oversized-over-short proportion you like. The jumper is the warmest piece you own, and with tights and a leather layer it holds up against the wind.

looks.title: Tank Over Tee
looks.idea: A slim white rib tank pulled over a faded band tee, with low-slung jeans, for an inside-out take on layering.
looks.howToWear: Put the boxy band tee on first, then pull the slim white tank over it. The tank should hug the body, with the black tee sleeves and the bottom hem showing around it, and the graphic partly visible. Wear the baggy jeans low and roll the hems once or twice so they sit above the chunky boot soles and stay clear of the bike chain. Put the cropped puffer on over everything with the chain outside it, and zip it to the chin against the wind.
looks.why: Layering the tank over the tee gives you a fitted shape over a boxy one, with a dark and light contrast that suits your colouring, and it looks like something you'd do on purpose. The band tee keeps the music-led side of your style, and the light-wash jeans lift the otherwise black outfit. It stays warm and bike-friendly, because the puffer, boots and rolled hems cover you for walking and cycling.

output.note: Your wardrobe has no scarf, beanie or gloves. At 4°C with a cold wind, those would help most on the bike, and any of them would fit with all three looks.

failures.detail: A bias-cut satin midi (l08) on a bike is the weak point. It narrows the stride and the hem can catch in the chain. 'Hitch it up through the hoodie' is a patch, not a solution. Tell her to knot or clip the hem, or to check her bike first.

The chain (l14) is worn over the hoodie but under the cropped puffer (l10). Once the puffer is zipped against the wind, the chain disappears. It needs to be worn with the puffer open indoors, or moved outside the puffer collar.

looks.comment: This is the real surprise and the right one. It takes the under-worn slip (l08) and puts it under her most-worn hoodie (l01), giving a three-hem stack of puffer, fleece and satin that is pure Berlin club and 90s grunge. Warmth holds up thanks to l13, l11 and l10. Only the cycling detail with the midi hem needs tightening.

failures.detail: A cable-knit jumper (l04) with a red tartan mini (l07) and retro low-tops (l12) leans campus prep, not grunge. The trainers make that worse rather than better. Her boots (l11) are what would keep this undone.
Picking up the jumper's green in the trainers (l12) is matchy. Combined with red tartan, it pushes the look towards the festive read the stylist claims to avoid.
Low-top leather and suede trainers (warmth 2/5) with only 80-denier tights leave the ankles exposed in a 4°C wind on a bike.
The idea line, 'looks like a worn-in 90s band tee', makes no sense for an outfit that has no band tee in it.

looks.comment: Red tartan, forest green and brown leather (l09) is a good palette for her contrast, and big-knit-over-mini is her proportion. But the trainers tip it into prep and leave her ankles cold. Swap them for l11 and the look becomes signable, but then it is close to her known gig outfit and much less of a surprise.

failures.detail: Band tee, baggy jeans, boots and puffer (l02, l05, l11, l10) is her everyday uniform. The tank-over-tee twist is the only new element in a 'surprise me' brief.
The puffer (l10) is zipped to the chin, so the tank-over-tee layering is invisible the whole time she is outside.
Under the puffer she has only a thin tee and a rib tank. A cropped puffer with low-slung jeans leaves a gap at the lower back when she leans forward on the bike in a cold 4°C wind.
A slim tank (l03) pulled over a boxy tee (l02) bunches the tee and covers the graphic. That undercuts the stylist's claim that this is the music-led piece.

looks.comment: This is the weakest look: her uniform with a styling trick that the outer layer hides. It also leaves her colder than it needs to be. It repeats l10, l11, l14 and l15 from Look 1, so the set feels narrower than it should.

judgement.missedOpportunity: The slip dress worn over trousers, not just under a hoodie: l02 band tee layered under l08 satin slip, over l06 black cargo trousers, with l11 boots, l10 puffer, l14 chain outside and l15 tote. It is a bigger surprise, very 90s and very Berlin club. It also solves both the cycling and the cold-leg problems, because she has trousers under the satin. And it keeps the band tee visible as the music signal.
judgement.summary: Look 1 is the standout. It gives the under-worn slip dress a real everyday life, it is true to her DNA, and it is warm enough. It is worth sending with a tighter fix for the midi hem on the bike. Look 2 has the right palette but tips into prep, with cold ankles from the trainers. Look 3 is her default outfit with a twist the puffer hides. Two of the three looks share most of their accessories and outerwear. The note about the missing scarf, beanie and gloves is honest and useful. Send Look 1, rework Look 2 with boots, and replace Look 3.

results.requestText: It's raining all day and I'll be walking a lot. What should I wear?

looks.title: Rainy Studio Day
looks.idea: The undone hoodie-and-cargo uniform, sealed against the weather by boots and a puffer.
looks.howToWear: Wear the oversized hoodie under the cropped puffer and pull the hood out over the puffer collar to keep rain off your neck. Leave the hoodie hem long so it peeks below the cropped puffer. Pull the cargo hems over the top of the boots so water runs off instead of in, or tuck them in if it's pouring. Wear the silver chain over the hoodie. Carry the tote close under your arm or inside your jacket line, as canvas soaks through.
looks.why: Cargos are the right call in cold rain: twill dries faster than denim and the hems won't drag. The oversized top over a short puffer fits your preferred proportions, and the black boots and puffer keep it grungy. It's easy to cycle in and has plenty of pockets for a day on the move.

looks.title: Tartan and Green
looks.idea: Your gig-night formula, swapped for a warmer top that makes red and deep green work together.
looks.howToWear: Pull the chunky green jumper loose over the tartan mini, with the hem sitting mid-hip and a little skirt showing beneath. Add the opaque tights and the lace-up boots, then the cropped puffer on top, left open so the green and red show. Wear the chain over the knit neckline.
looks.why: It follows the spirit of your favourite outfit: oversized top, short skirt, tights, boots. The wool jumper and skirt give real warmth at 3°C, and red and deep green are both strong colours on you. The short skirt keeps the oversized knit balanced, and tights plus boots keep you covered and warm on the bike.

looks.title: Slip and Tee Grunge
looks.idea: A 90s grunge layer of satin slip over a band tee, made weatherproof with tights and boots.
looks.howToWear: Wear the faded band tee under the slip dress, so the boxy sleeves and hem show at the neckline and the boxy shape sits under the bias cut. Add the opaque tights and boots, then the puffer zipped over everything. Wear the silver chain over the tee. If cycling, let the midi skirt fall over the saddle and keep the puffer closed against wind.
looks.why: This is the most night-ready look: satin against faded cotton and chunky boots is classic Berlin club and grunge. The tee and tights add warmth to a dress that would otherwise be too thin for November. It's a different route to your style, built on mixing soft and rough.

output.note: Your leather jacket and the suede-and-leather trainers aren't used because both would be ruined or soaked in all-day cold rain. The puffer is your only real weather layer, so it appears in every look. Jeans are skipped because wet hems at 3°C get cold and heavy. Missing from the wardrobe: a waterproof shell or umbrella and a rain-proof bag, as the canvas tote will get wet.

failures.detail: Telling her to leave the l01 cotton-fleece hem long below the cropped l10 means the most absorbent fabric in the look sits exactly where the rain runs off the puffer. The cotton hood pulled out over the collar will also soak through within an hour of walking, and nothing warns her about it.
At 3°C with wet wind on a bike, l06 cotton twill alone is thin on the legs. The obvious fix was l13 tights worn under the cargos as a base layer, and it was missed.

looks.comment: This is the correct answer to the brief: cargo hems over the l11 boots and the l10 puffer as the only weather layer, all in her own idiom. The hood-out tip and the bag warning are useful. It needed one more warmth move to be excellent: l13 tights under l06, or l03 as a base layer under l01.

failures.detail: 'Puffer left open so the green and red show' in all-day cold rain means the l04 wool-blend cable knit soaks and stays heavy and cold all day. Styling for display has overridden the weather.
Legs are covered only by 80-denier l13 tights. Walking and cycling all day in 3°C rain, they will be wet, wind-chilled and laddered by the bike.

A red tartan mini with a forest-green cable knit tips towards festive or preppy, which is the exact thing her DNA rejects. The l02 band tee or the l01 hoodie in her proven formula keeps it grunge. This swap isn't argued, just asserted.

looks.comment: A reasonable instinct to warm up her proven gig formula. But this is a dry-cold look, not a rain look. The open-puffer instruction is wrong for the day, and the green-plus-tartan pairing drifts preppy without the stylist acknowledging it.

failures.detail: Black satin l08 is the most rain-vulnerable fabric in the wardrobe. It water-spots, clings cold when wet, and the midi hem hangs below the cropped l10 straight into the rain.
A bias-cut satin midi is slippery on a saddle and close to the chain. 'Let the skirt fall over the saddle' is not a real cycling solution for a day of riding in wind and rain.
It is pitched as 'the most night-ready look', but the brief is a wet day of walking. Nobody asked for a night look.

The stylist's own note rejects l09 and l12 for rain damage and rejects l05 for wet hems, then sends satin with a dragging midi hem. The logic is inconsistent, and 'sleeves and hem show at the neckline' doesn't make sense.

looks.comment: A good grunge layering idea that genuinely suits her, on entirely the wrong day. This is forced variety, and it should have been cut or kept for a dry evening.

judgement.missedOpportunity: The best wet-day answer is a better-insulated version of Look 1: l13 tights under l06 cargos as a hidden thermal layer, l03 tank as a base under l01 hoodie (the hood is the only head cover she has), l10 puffer zipped, cargo hems over l11 boots, l14 chain, and l15 tote with a bin liner inside. A strong alternative was l04 under l10 instead of l01, because wool stays warm when damp where cotton fleece doesn't. Separately, the honest second look was her proven gig formula of l01, l07, l13 and l11, offered only with a warning about wet tights, not the open-puffer green-knit version.
judgement.summary: Look 1 and the stylist's note are strong. The note is genuinely helpful and honest about what the wardrobe lacks: a waterproof shell and a rainproof bag. Looks 2 and 3, though, are styled for a cold dry day and ignore 'raining all day, walking a lot.' Look 2 leaves the puffer open over a wool knit with only tights on the legs, and Look 3 sends satin and a midi hem into the rain and onto a bike. With a wardrobe this small and weather this hard, the right package was one excellent, thoroughly weatherproofed look plus one honest variant. Three looks with two that don't hold up in the rain is padding. Fix the warmth on Look 1, cut Look 3, and rework Look 2 before sending.

results.requestText: First date — cocktails at a smart bar.

looks.title: Slip and Leather
looks.idea: Black satin slip against beat-up leather: the dressed-up look that still feels like her.
looks.howToWear: Wear the slip dress over the 80 denier tights with the chunky boots so the satin looks edgy, not precious. Put the leather jacket on over it and leave it unzipped with the sleeves pushed up slightly. Wear the chain at the neckline. The puffer goes over everything for the cycle and comes off at the bar. Keep the tote for your things.
looks.why: It's the most date-ready option in her wardrobe, and the slip dress has only been worn 3 times. Satin with worn leather and chunky boots keeps it grunge, not polished. The bias-cut midi works on a bike with tights underneath, and the boots and puffer cover the 4°C wind.

looks.title: Green Knit, Red Tartan
looks.idea: Deep green and red on a short skirt: her gig-night formula, turned up for a date.
looks.howToWear: Pull the oversized green jumper on over the tartan mini, tucking only the front few centimetres of hem so the skirt peeks out under the knit. Add the opaque tights and lace-up boots. Wear the chain over the knit's neckline. Wear the puffer for the ride and take it off inside.
looks.why: It follows the shape of her favourite gig outfit: oversized top, short tartan skirt, black tights, boots. Forest green and red both flatter her high-contrast colouring. The big knit against a short skirt is the proportion she likes, and the wool and tights keep her warm on the bike. It uses the tartan skirt, which she's worn only 6 times.

looks.title: Cargo Night
looks.idea: Relaxed black cargos with a bare white tank and leather: low-key Berlin, with the skin and chain doing the date work.
looks.howToWear: Tuck the white ribbed tank into the cargos, leaving the waistband slightly slouchy. Put the leather jacket on open over it. Wear the chain over the tank so it's visible. Wear the retro white and green trainers with the cargo hems stacked at the ankle. Wear the puffer over everything for the cycle and take it off at the bar.
looks.why: This is the easy, undone option. The fitted tank balances the baggy trousers, and the white against black leather is sharp on her colouring. The trainers are the most comfortable shoe for a long cycle. It's the least dressy of the three, but the chain and clean tank make it look deliberate.

output.note: Her wardrobe has nothing truly smart, which suits her style anyway. The slip dress look is the most dressed-up. If the bar is strict about trainers, choose look 1 or 2, which both have boots.

failures.detail: The boxy, hip-length l09 leather jacket under the cropped l10 puffer means the leather hangs below the puffer hem and the puffer won't close over it. Two jackets on a bike is bulky, and she then has to manage both at the bar.

The large canvas tote l15 is the clunkiest note on a first date at a smart bar. The stylist should say plainly that the wardrobe lacks a small evening bag and suggest carrying the tote half-empty or folded down.
There is no word on how the bias-cut satin behaves on a bike (riding up, catching on the chain) or how to manage it. 'Most date-ready' is asserted rather than shown.

looks.comment: Right anchor: l08 is the only piece that answers 'smart bar', and roughing it up with l13, l11 and l14 keeps it hers. The leather-plus-puffer stacking is a practical misstep: pick one outer layer, or put warmth under the satin instead.

failures.detail: This is her gig uniform with l04 swapped in for l01. A chunky cable knit and a canvas tote read cosy-casual, not smart-bar date. Nothing in the look is lifted beyond the chain.
Forest green cable knit over a red tartan mini in mid-November tips towards festive. The explanation doesn't address how to stop the red-plus-green reading as Christmas.
It leans almost entirely on the proven formula rather than finding a date-specific idea.

looks.comment: Very much Lena, warm and bike-proof, and the front-tuck to show the l07 hem is a good move. But it's a gig outfit relabelled for a date rather than one sharpened for a smart bar.

failures.detail: A white rib tank l03, cargos l06 and low-top trainers l12 at a 'smart bar' is the most casual combination in her wardrobe. The stylist admits it's the least dressy and that trainers may be refused at the door.
The l12 low-tops (warmth 2/5) on a 4°C windy cycle mean cold feet. A thin tank plus open leather is also cold the moment the puffer comes off near the door.
The same double-jacket problem as look 1: hip-length l09 under the cropped l10.
This is a daytime basics formula with a chain added, not a date idea.

looks.comment: Coherent as a daytime look, but it doesn't answer a first date at a smart bar. It's filler to reach three looks, and the stylist's own caveat about trainers concedes this.

judgement.missedOpportunity: Pull the oversized forest green jumper l04 over the black satin slip l08 so the bias-cut satin swings below the knit: the classic 90s grunge knit-over-slip. Add l13 tights, l11 boots and the l14 chain over the knit's neckline, with only the l10 puffer for the ride. It's warmer and more bike-friendly than satin under leather, and it hits her oversized-over-fluid proportion and her high-contrast green. It reads more dressed than look 2 while staying undone. Alternatively, put the l02 band tee under the l08 slip for a club-style take.
judgement.summary: The stylist found the right anchor in the under-worn slip dress l08, and look 1 is a credible date look for her. However, both l08 and l06 are styled with leather jacket l09 stacked under a cropped puffer l10, which is clumsy for cycling. Look 2 is essentially her known gig outfit and doesn't rise to 'smart bar'. Look 3 is too casual and too cold-footed for the brief. The honest note that the wardrobe has nothing truly smart is good. It should also have said there's no evening bag, and it missed the strongest move: green knit over the satin slip.

results.requestText: Weekend brunch and then wandering around the shops.

looks.title: Green Knit, Cropped Puffer
looks.idea: Cosy oversized knit against baggy denim, with the green picked up again in the trainers.
